method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: Why did Bacon think words obstruct the understanding?
What two kinds of verbal error did Bacon distinguish?
Why did Locke devote a book of the Essay to language?
What was the linguistic turn in philosophy?

Locke devotes Book III of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding to language. This is a strong indication that Locke thinks issues about language were of considerable importance in attaining knowledge.
Without general terms and classes we would be faced with the impossible task of trying to know a vast world of particulars.
He also rejects the claim that there is a single classification of things in nature that the natural philosopher should seek to discover.

“Locke’s main semantic thesis”
Kretzmann, however, argues persuasively that Locke distinguishes between meaning and reference and that ideas provide the meaning but not the reference of words.
When I say, ‘the sun is the cause of the day’, I do not mean that my idea of the sun causes or excites in me the idea of day
What is novel is the idea that what had been seen as philosophical claims were better understood as proposals for structuring the language of science.
